ingredients.rawText: A scant 1/2 cup (about 2 ounces/60 g) unskinned almonds
1 whole (about 4 pounds/1.8 kg) boneless turkey breast with skin on, the 2 halves cut apart, netting removed
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground cinnamon, preferably Mexican canela
A scant 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground cloves
1 slice firm white bread, darkly toasted and broken into several pieces
ingredients.item: firm white bread, darkly toasted and broken up

ingredients.rawText: 1 ounce (30 g) Mexican chocolate, roughly chopped
Sprigs of watercress or fresh flat-leaf parsley, for garnish
ingredients.item: watercress or flat-leaf parsley sprigs, for garnish

instructions.text: Set out all the ingredients and do the basic prep first: husk and rinse the tomatillos, stem and seed the dried chiles, peel the garlic, grind the spices, toast the bread, and chop the chocolate.

Roast the tomatillos under a very hot broiler about 4 inches from the heat until blackened in spots, roughly 5 minutes per side, then scrape them with their juices into a large bowl. In a dry skillet, toast the sesame seeds until golden, about 5 minutes, and stir two-thirds of them into the tomatillos, saving the rest for garnish.

Melt the lard (or heat the oil) in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Working in batches of 3 or 4, fry the torn chile pieces just 20-30 seconds per batch, until the interior lightens - don't let them scorch or the mole will turn bitter. Lift them out with a slotted spoon into a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them soak about 30 minutes.

In the same fat, fry the garlic and almonds until browned, about 5 minutes, then the raisins for 20-30 seconds until puffed; add both to the tomatillo bowl, draining off excess fat each time. Raise the heat and brown the turkey breast halves on all sides, about 10 minutes each, then set them aside (refrigerate if not continuing within the hour).

Drain the soaked chiles (reserving the soaking liquid if it isn't bitter) and blend them smooth with about 2 1/4 cups of that liquid or fresh water, then press the puree through a strainer. Blend the tomatillo mixture with 1 cup water, the cinnamon, pepper, anise, cloves, toasted bread and chocolate, and strain that too.

Reheat the pot with a thin film of fat, add the chile puree, and stir frequently until it darkens and thickens to a paste consistency, 10-15 minutes. Stir in the tomatillo puree and continue cooking until thickened again, another 5-10 minutes.

Stir in 6 cups water, partially cover, and simmer gently over medium-low for 45 minutes, adjusting the consistency with a little water if it gets too thick, or extra simmering if too thin. Season with salt and the sugar to taste.

Heat the oven to 325°F. Nestle the turkey into the mole, cover, and bake until an instant-read thermometer reads 150°F in the center, about 40 minutes (a bit longer if the turkey went in cold from the fridge).

Rest the turkey under foil for 10 minutes, then slice it 1/2-inch thick and arrange on a warm platter. Thin the mole with a little water if needed, taste and adjust salt or sugar, then ladle 3-4 cups of sauce over the turkey and sprinkle with the reserved sesame seeds. Garnish with watercress or parsley.

R0420.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Rick Bayless's website (rickbayless.com), adapted from his book Mexico One Plate at a Time, 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. instructions.text: Blend the eggs, milk, water, flour and melted butter together for about 10 seconds until smooth. Chill the batter for 1 hour so trapped air bubbles can settle - this keeps the crepes from tearing as they cook. The batter keeps up to 48 hours refrigerated.

Heat a small nonstick pan and coat it with butter. Pour about 1 ounce of batter into the center, swirling to coat the pan evenly. Cook about 30 seconds, flip, and cook another 10 seconds, then slide onto a cutting board to cool flat. Repeat with the remaining batter, buttering the pan as needed.
Once cooled, stack the crepes and store in sealed bags in the fridge for several days, or freeze up to 2 months; thaw frozen crepes on a rack before peeling apart.

R0156.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Food Network (Alton Brown, Good Eats episode 'Crepe Expectations'), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. For a savory batch, add 1/4 teaspoon salt plus 1/4 cup chopped herbs, spinach or sun-dried tomatoes; for sweet, add 2 1/2 tablespoons sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla and 2 tablespoons of a favorite liqueur.

ingredients.rawText: 4 skin-on salmon fillets, about 6 ounces (170 g) each
ingredients.item: skin-on salmon fillets, about 6 ounces each

ingredients.rawText: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions.text: Press the salmon fillets between paper towels to dry thoroughly, then season all sides with salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a large stainless, cast iron, or carbon steel skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Lay in a fillet skin side down and press it firmly with the back of a flexible fish spatula for about 10 seconds to keep the skin from buckling; add the remaining fillets one at a time, pressing each the same way.

Cook, pressing occasionally to keep good contact with the pan, until the skin releases easily and is crisp, about 4 minutes; if it still sticks when you try to lift a corner, give it more time. Continue cooking until the center reaches 110°F for rare, 120°F for medium-rare, or 130°F for medium, 5 to 7 minutes total.
Flip the fillets with the spatula and a fork and cook the second side for just about 15 seconds, then transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain briefly before serving.

R0093.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Serious Eats (J. Kenji Lopez-Alt), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Cooking the salmon almost all the way through skin-side down renders the fat and keeps the flesh from overcooking.

ingredients.rawText: 1 pound (455 g) fresh-ground corn masa for tortillas, or 1 3/4 cups (225 g) powdered masa harina for tortillas (such as Maseca brand) mixed with 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons (270 ml) hot tap water
ingredients.item: fresh-ground corn masa for tortillas, or 1 3/4 cups masa harina mixed with 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons hot water

instructions.text: Set up a heavy griddle or two skillets at two temperatures - one side (or pan) at medium to medium-low, the other at medium-high.
Knead the masa with just enough water to make a soft, non-sticky dough, similar to soft cookie dough.

Line a tortilla press with a square of plastic, center a walnut-sized ball of dough on it, cover with a second sheet of plastic, and press to flatten into a 5-6 inch disk. Rotate the covered disk 180 degrees and press again lightly to even the thickness.
Peel off the top plastic sheet, flip the tortilla onto your palm lining up its top edge with your fingertip, then peel off the remaining plastic starting from the top.
Lay the tortilla onto the cooler side of the griddle by sweeping your hand away and letting the dangling edge catch first, then rolling your hand out from under it - don't just drop it off your palm.
Cook 15-30 seconds on the cooler side, just until the tortilla releases and looks slightly dry at the edge.

Move it to the hotter side and cook until splotchy brown underneath, 30-45 seconds, then flip again and cook another 30-45 seconds to brown the other side - the tortilla should puff up like pita during these final seconds.
Transfer to a cloth-lined basket, stacking and keeping the tortillas covered as you go so the trapped steam finishes softening them.

R0097.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Rick Bayless's website (rickbayless.com), adapted from his book Mexico One Plate at a Time, 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Yields about 15 tortillas.

2/3 cup potato starch or corn starch

Grapeseed oil (or vegetable oil, peanut oil), for deep-frying

instructions.text: Cut the tip off each wing and chop the wing in half, yielding about 3 pounds and 24-26 pieces. Mix the wings by hand with the salt, pepper and ginger, then dip and press each piece in the starch to coat evenly.

For the sauce, heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet or wok over medium-high, add the garlic and dried chilies (if using), and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in the soy sauce, rice syrup, vinegar and mustard and let it bubble a few minutes, then add the brown sugar, stir, and remove from the heat.

Heat about 4 cups of oil to 330-350°F. Slide the starch-coated wings in one at a time and deep-fry, turning occasionally, for about 12-13 minutes, then drain in a strainer or on a rack and let rest a few minutes with the heat off.

Reheat the oil and fry the wings a second time for another 10-12 minutes, until deep golden and very crunchy. Fry in batches if needed. If using peanuts, fry them separately in a small strainer for 15-30 seconds until light golden, then set aside.

R0322.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Maangchi's dakgangjeong (crispy Korean fried chicken) recipe, 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. This card is the first half of a two-part scan; see the continuation card for coating the fried chicken in the sauce.

instructions.text: Once the chicken is fried and crunchy, reheat the seasoning sauce until it bubbles.
Add the hot fried chicken (and the fried peanuts, if using) to the sauce and mix well with a wooden spoon so everything is evenly coated.

Transfer the coated chicken to a serving platter, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and serve right away. It stays crunchy even the next day and doesn't need a dipping sauce, though it pairs well with baek-kimchi (white kimchi).

instructions.text: Chop the cauliflower into small florets, rinse well, and place in a bowl. Add enough hot water to cover the florets, then cover and blanch for 15-20 minutes.

Meanwhile, soak the dry red chilies in 1/4 cup warm water for 15 minutes. In a small grinder, blend the soaked chilies with the chopped garlic, chopped ginger, and 1-2 tablespoons water into a smooth paste.

Drain the blanched cauliflower well and transfer to a mixing bowl. Add the red chili paste and mix well, then add the gram flour, rice flour, and corn starch, followed by the turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and coriander powder.

Add the lemon juice and 1/3 cup water, then season with salt and mix everything together thoroughly. The batter should coat the florets without being runny or dry - adjust with a little more water or gram flour as needed. Cover and let marinate for 20-30 minutes.

Heat 7-8 tablespoons oil in a kadai or deep skillet until medium hot (about 350-356°F/175-180°C). Working in batches so as not to overcrowd, carefully place the battered florets in the oil and fry on one side until golden and crisp, then turn with a slotted spoon and fry the other side, turning as needed until evenly golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
For the tempering, remove excess oil from the kadai, leaving about 2 teaspoons (or use fresh oil). Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add the dry red chilies and fry until they darken.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves, and saute until the onions turn translucent. Season with salt and, if desired, a pinch of sugar to balance the heat.
Add the fried cauliflower florets and immediately switch off the heat. Toss to coat evenly, then stir in the chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with coconut chutney, coriander-mint chutney, or tomato ketchup, alongside roti or bread if desired.

ingredients.rawText: 1 large globe eggplant (about 2 pounds), sliced 1/2"-3/4" thick

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 450°F. Drizzle the eggplant slices with half the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast on a sheet pan, flipping halfway through, until custardy-soft and browned on both sides, about 25-30 minutes.

ingredients.rawText: 120 grams (4 ounces) ground meat (pork, chicken or turkey)
1/2 teaspoon ginger, minced (or 1/4 teaspoon ginger powder)
2 teaspoons Sichuan peppercorns (up to 3 teaspoons for extra numbing)
3 tablespoons Doubanjiang (reduce to 2 tbsp for less salty/spicy)

instructions.text: Combine the ground meat with the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and ginger; mix well and set aside as the marinade.
Stir the cornstarch with 1 tablespoon water in a small bowl and set aside as a slurry.
Heat the oil with the Sichuan peppercorns in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until the peppercorns are dark and crisp, then scoop them out onto a paper towel and reserve for garnish.

Spread the tofu over the meat without stirring immediately. Add the chili oil, five-spice powder, and sugar, then pour in the water and bring to a simmer. Cover and simmer 10-15 minutes until the tofu is tender and the sauce has reduced by about half; taste and adjust seasoning.
Grind the reserved fried Sichuan peppercorns in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle.
Re-stir the cornstarch slurry and swirl it into the skillet, stirring gently until the sauce thickens. Turn off the heat and transfer to a serving bowl.

instructions.text: Position a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 400°F. Oil a 10-inch springform pan, line the bottom with parchment, and oil the parchment too.

ingredients.rawText: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, washed and soaked in 2 1/2 cups cold water for 3 to 4 hours, until soft
1/4 cup sugar (white or brown, or swerve)
1 medium Korean radish (8-12 oz) or daikon, peeled
2 pounds beef short ribs (8 pieces), rinsed and soaked in cold water 30 min-1 hr
12 pine nuts, tips removed (optional, for garnish)
12 frozen ginkgo nuts, shelled and cooked (optional, for garnish)

instructions.text: Drain the soaked shiitake mushrooms, reserving 2 cups of the soaking liquid (topping up with cold water if needed). Whisk the soy sauce, mirim, sugar, black pepper, garlic, and ginger into the soaking liquid to make the seasoning sauce.
Trim the stems from the mushrooms and quarter the caps. Cut the radish and carrots into 1 1/2-inch cubes and round the edges into roughly 1-inch balls, about 10-12 of each.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the soaked and drained ribs, and blanch 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Drain, rinse well with cold water, and wash out the pot.
Return the ribs to the pot with the seasoning sauce, cover, and cook over medium-high heat for 20 minutes.
Stir in the mushrooms, chestnuts, radish, and carrots. Cover, reduce heat to low, and cook 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the jujubes and rice syrup, cover, and simmer another 10 minutes or until the meat is nearly falling off the bone (add about a cup of water and cook longer if the ribs are still tough).
Raise the heat to high and spoon the pan juices over the meat and vegetables for a few minutes until the sauce reduces and everything is nicely glazed.
Transfer to a platter, sprinkle with the pine nuts and ginkgo nuts if using, and serve with rice and side dishes.

ingredients.rawText: 1 large head of cabbage (about 3 lbs.) - or use 2 smaller heads
3/4 cup uncooked long grain rice (brown or white)
1 cup Pomi strained tomatoes or canned tomato puree
3/4 cup liquid (beef stock, cabbage water, or combined with leftover tomato)
ingredients.item: beef stock or cabbage cooking water

instructions.text: Boil a large pot of water. Cut the core out of the cabbage and simmer it core-side down, covered, for 10 minutes.

While the cabbage simmers, saute the onion and garlic in the olive oil over medium-high heat 3-5 minutes until browned, then add the mushrooms and cook 2 more minutes. Cool the mixture in a large bowl.

Remove the cabbage to a baking sheet, keeping the pot water. Peel off the leaves, trimming the thick center spine, setting aside the best 16 whole leaves (return the core to the water briefly if it's still too firm to peel).
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Mix the cooled onion mixture with the ground sirloin, uncooked rice, parsley, tomato, salt, and pepper.

Spoon about 1/4 cup of filling onto each cabbage leaf, roll up, and arrange seam-side down in a 13x9-inch pan. Pour the reserved liquid over the rolls, top with a few leftover leaves, cover tightly with foil, and bake 1 1/2 hours (set the pan on a baking sheet in case it drips).
Let rest 30 minutes after baking, or cool and refrigerate overnight for best flavor; they also freeze well. Serve plain or browned in a little oil with sour cream on the side.

ingredients.rawText: 2 cups (8 ounces) coarsely shredded cooked chicken
5 ounces (1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) pork lard or vegetable shortening
1 pound fresh-ground corn masa for tamales, or 1 3/4 cups dried masa harina mixed with 3/4 cup hot water
ingredients.item: fresh corn masa for tamales (or masa harina mixed with hot water)

instructions.text: Soak the corn husks in hot water, weighted down so they stay submerged, for about two hours until pliable.
Broil the tomatillos, unpeeled garlic, and chiles on a baking sheet about 4 inches below the heat for around 6 minutes, until softened and blackened in spots; flip and roast the other side.
Let everything cool, peel the garlic, then puree the tomatillos, garlic, and chiles (with any collected juices) to a coarse consistency in a blender or food processor.
Stir the shredded chicken and chopped cilantro into the puree and season with salt; this is the filling.
With an electric mixer, beat the lard (or shortening) with the salt and baking powder until light and fluffy.

Beat in the masa in three additions, then gradually add chicken broth until the batter reaches the consistency of a soft, spreadable cake batter. Keep beating until a small dollop of batter floats when dropped in a cup of cold water.
Set up a steamer with about an inch of water in the bottom and line the rack with leftover corn husk scraps.
Pat the soaked husks dry. Spread about 1/4 cup of masa batter into a roughly 4-inch square on each husk, leaving borders on the sides, then spoon filling down the center.

Fold the long sides of the husk over the filling and fold up the tapered end to close the bottom, leaving the top open; tie loosely with a strip of husk or string if desired, and stand the tamales upright in the steamer.
Cover with more husk scraps, cover the steamer, and steam over a steady simmer for about 1 to 1 1/4 hours, adding boiling water as needed to keep the steam going.
Test one tamal — it is done when the husk peels away cleanly from the masa; steam a bit longer if it still sticks. Let the tamales rest 10-15 minutes before serving.

ingredients.rawText: 1 teaspoon sugar (for yeast) plus 1 cup sugar (for batter)
1 tablespoon ghee or coconut oil, plus more for greasing

instructions.text: Rinse the uncooked rice a couple of times, then soak it in water for 4-6 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and blend it with the cooked rice, grated coconut, and enough cold water to make a smooth batter.
Dissolve the teaspoon of sugar in the warm water, stir in the yeast, and let it proof for about 10 minutes until foamy.

Add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli powder, pepper powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and fennel powder, adding a little extra oil if needed, and saute for 3-4 minutes.
Add the sliced tomato and saute until softened and cooked.
Pour in the medium-thick coconut milk, season with salt, and stir well.
Add the boiled egg halves to the gravy and let it simmer for about 10 minutes so the masala coats the eggs.
Stir in the thick coconut milk and gently swirl the pan without breaking the eggs; once it comes back to a boil and reaches the desired consistency, turn off the heat.

ingredients.rawText: All purpose flour/Maida - 1 cup + 1 tbsp for tossing the soaked fruits
Rum/brandy/red wine - enough to soak the fruit
ingredients.item: rum, brandy, or red wine (for soaking)

instructions.text: A week or more ahead, chop the dried fruits and nuts and soak them in rum, brandy, or wine in a sealed jar at room temperature, shaking occasionally; the longer they soak, the better the flavor.

To make the caramel, heat sugar with a tablespoon of water in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat without stirring (swirl the pan occasionally) until it turns a darker golden brown, then remove from heat and carefully stir in the half cup of water. Let the caramel cool before using.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and sift together the flour and baking powder.
Separate the egg yolks from the whites; whisk the yolks with the vanilla in a small bowl.
Cream the butter and sugar together until light and well combined.
Beat in the yolk mixture gradually, alternating with spoonfuls of the sifted flour, until smooth.
Beat in the cooled caramel and the spice powders (caraway, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves) until well combined.
Gently fold in the remaining flour by hand until just incorporated - don't overmix, to keep the cake tender.
Drain the soaked fruit, set aside about half a cup, and fold the rest into the batter.
Toss the reserved half cup of fruit with a tablespoon of flour to help prevent it from sinking.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the batter until just combined.
Pour the batter into a greased, parchment-lined 9-inch pan, scattering the flour-tossed fruit over the top and smoothing it in.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool the cake in the pan for 10-15 minutes, then poke a few holes in the top and drizzle over a teaspoon or two of rum, brandy, or wine before turning it out onto a rack to cool completely.

instructions.text: Take the lamb loin chops out of the refrigerator about 30 minutes before cooking so they come to room temperature.
Mix 3 tablespoons olive oil with the minced garlic, salt and pepper in a small bowl, then rub the mixture all over the chops.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chops about 3 minutes per side.
Lower the heat, flip the chops back to the first side, and let them finish cooking gently for about 5 more minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat, cover, and let the chops rest in the pan for 10-15 minutes.
Check for doneness -- the center should be pink and register about 145F. If needed, continue cooking covered over medium heat a few more minutes.
Garnish with chopped parsley and pomegranate seeds before serving.

instructions.text: The day before serving, score the leg of lamb deeply in a crosshatch pattern on both sides with a sharp knife.
Grind the cumin, coriander seeds, peppercorns and cardamom seeds together in a spice grinder or with a pestle and mortar.
Combine the ground spices in a large bowl with the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, almonds, lemon juice, chilli powder, cinnamon and salt to make the marinade.
Rub the marinade all over the lamb, working it into the scored grooves. Transfer to a large food bag or covered casserole dish and refrigerate overnight.

About 3 hours before serving, preheat the oven to 180C/350F/gas 4. Put the lamb in a deep roasting tray with 125ml water, cover loosely with foil, and roast for about 2 1/4 hours for pink lamb (2 1/2 hours for more well done).
About 45 minutes before the lamb is due to finish, add the unpeeled shallots to the tray and drizzle lightly with oil. With 20 minutes left, remove the foil so the lamb browns.
Take the lamb out of the oven, cover with foil, and let it rest 15-20 minutes before carving.

ingredients.rawText: 2 skin-on salmon fillets (3/4 lb, 340 g total; less than 1 inch/2.5 cm thick; 4-6 oz/113-170 g per fillet)
1/2 tsp toasted white and black sesame seeds (optional garnish)

instructions.text: Check the salmon fillets for pin bones and scales, removing any with tweezers or a knife.
Whisk together the miso, sake, mirin, soy sauce and sesame oil in a bowl or shallow dish to make the marinade.
Cut the salmon into individual portions if needed, then place skin-side up in the marinade and spoon it over the flesh and sides to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 1-2 hours (up to 3 hours for a thicker cut). Avoid marinating overnight, as the fish can become too salty.
Preheat the broiler to high with the rack about 9 inches from the heating element. Line a baking sheet with foil and oil it lightly.
Wipe the excess marinade off the salmon so it doesn't burn, then place the fillets skin-side down on the baking sheet.

ingredients.rawText: 1 large onion OR 2 medium sized onions, thinly sliced
1/4 teaspoon black pepper powder (kali mirch powder)

instructions.text: Rinse the mushrooms well, trim the stalk ends, and chop them. Thinly slice the onion and slit the green chilies.
Heat the oil in a pan or wok and add the onions with a pinch of salt (this speeds up softening). Saute, stirring often, until they just turn light golden -- keep them soft, not browned or crisp.

instructions.text: Pat the pork tenderloins dry with paper towels.

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a pan and saute the chopped onions until translucent and light pink.

instructions.text: Gather the ingredients. Combine the dashi, mirin, sake and soy sauce in a bowl, then stir in the sugar until dissolved -- this is the seasoning mixture.
Thinly slice the onion and chop the mitsuba or green onion. Slice the chicken thigh diagonally into roughly 1.5-inch pieces so it cooks quickly and evenly.

Taste the broth and adjust if needed, then slowly drizzle the beaten egg over the chicken and onion. Cover and cook on medium-low until the egg is set to your liking -- traditionally still slightly runny.
Scatter the mitsuba or green onion over the top just before taking it off the heat.
Slide the chicken and egg mixture over a bowl of steamed rice, spoon over any remaining sauce, and serve with shichimi togarashi on the side if you like.

ingredients.rawText: 1 (12 to 14-ounce / 340 to 400g) block of extra firm tofu, drained

instructions.text: Tear the tofu by hand into 1-inch chunks and place in a large bowl.

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 cups/181 grams all-purpose flour, plus more for the work surface
1/2 cup/113 grams (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces, at room temperature
5 cups/750 grams strawberries (about 2 quarts), hulled and halved
1 tablespoon/14.5 grams fresh lime or lemon juice
2 tablespoons/27.5 grams light brown sugar (for topping)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

For the shortcakes, whisk together the flour, cornmeal, both sugars, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Work the butter in with your hands until no large pieces remain, then mix in the cream just until the dough comes together. Turn it onto a floured surface and knead briefly, about 2 minutes, until it's no longer very sticky.

Pat the dough into a circle about 1 inch thick and cut out rounds with a 2-inch cutter (a glass works too). Gather and re-pat the scraps to cut more rounds. Set the shortcakes aside (chilling them if the kitchen is warm) while you prepare the filling.

For the filling, toss the strawberries with the granulated sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice in a bowl. Spread the fruit in a 9-inch cast-iron skillet, pie dish or cake pan, then arrange the shortcake rounds on top.

Brush the tops of the shortcakes with cream and sprinkle with the remaining brown sugar. Bake until the shortcakes are golden and the strawberry juices have thickened and are bubbling at the edges, about 25 to 30 minutes.
Let the cobbler cool slightly before serving so the juices have a chance to set and the first bite doesn't scald.

R0208.title: Strawberry Shortcake Cobbler

ingredients.rawText: 200 g azuki beans (about 7 oz, a little less than 1 cup)
Water, as needed for soaking and cooking
Pinch of salt (kosher or sea salt)

instructions.text: Rinse the azuki beans well and soak them in plenty of water overnight, about 8 to 12 hours.
Drain the soaked beans and place them in a large pot with enough water to cover by 1-2 inches (the beans will roughly double in volume as they cook, so use a big pot). Bring to a boil.
Once boiling, turn off the heat, cover, and let the beans sit for 5 minutes, then drain them in a sieve and discard that water.
Return the beans to the pot, add fresh water just to cover, and bring to a boil again. Reduce to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.

Simmer the beans for over an hour, occasionally pushing them back under the water with a slotted spoon and topping up water as it evaporates so the beans stay just covered (too much water can cause them to move around and break apart). The beans are done when one squeezes easily between your fingers.

Raise the heat to high and stir in the sugar in three additions, stirring constantly. Keep cooking and stirring until you can draw a line across the bottom of the pot with a spatula and the trail holds for a couple of seconds, then stir in the salt and remove from the heat (the paste will thicken further as it cools).
Transfer the paste to a container to cool rather than leaving it in the hot pot. Once cool, cover and refrigerate for up to about a week, or portion and freeze for up to a month.

Let the pressure release naturally for about 15 minutes, then release any remaining pressure and open the lid.
Shred the pork with two forks, then lift it out with a slotted spoon onto a baking sheet, discarding the citrus rinds and cooking liquid (or reserving liquid if you like it juicier).
Taste and add a little more salt if needed, then broil the pork for about 3-5 minutes, watching closely, until the edges are browned and crisp.

Meanwhile, make the pickled onions: pour boiling water over the sliced onions in a bowl, let sit briefly, then drain. Heat the vinegar, lime juice, sugar, salt and red pepper flakes in a small pan until the sugar dissolves, adjust sweetness to taste, then pour over the onions. Warm the corn tortillas, then fill with the crispy carnitas and top with sliced avocado, cilantro and pickled onions; serve with extra lime wedges.

instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the ground turkey, bread crumbs, onion, parsley, eggs, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, basil, oregano, about 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.

instructions.text: Preheat the air fryer to 380°F and lightly mist the basket with non-stick spray.
Slice each chicken breast in half lengthwise to make 4 thin cutlets, then pound each between plastic wrap to an even 1/4-inch thickness.

Set up a dredging station: flour mixed with half the paprika/garlic powder/onion powder/salt/pepper in one bowl, the whisked eggs in a second bowl, and the panko mixed with the remaining seasoning in a third.
Coat each cutlet in the seasoned flour, shaking off the excess, dip into the egg wash, then press firmly into the seasoned panko on both sides so the crumbs adhere well.
Arrange the cutlets in a single layer in the air fryer basket without overlapping and cook at 380°F for 6 minutes.
Flip the cutlets, raise the temperature to 400°F, and cook another 2-3 minutes until golden and the internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Let the cutlets rest for a couple of minutes before serving, with lemon wedges if desired.

Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge up to 4 days (best within the first two). Reheat in the air fryer at 325°F for 5-10 minutes to restore crispness, or microwave for 30-90 seconds if in a hurry (won't stay crispy). Uncooked breaded cutlets can be frozen in a single layer and cooked from frozen with a couple of extra minutes; avoid freezing already-cooked cutlets, as the breading won't recover.

instructions.text: Make the filling: blend the guajillo chiles, garlic, black pepper, and cumin with 3 cups water until smooth, then strain through a medium-mesh strainer into a saucepan.

Add the pork, another 3 cups water, and 1 teaspoon salt. Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pork is fork-tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick sauce, about 1 hour. Shred the pork with a fork, season with more salt if needed, and let cool.

Make the batter: beat the lard with 2 teaspoons salt and the baking powder until light, about 1 minute. Beat in the masa in three additions, then reduce speed and mix in 1 cup of the broth. Continue beating until a small dollop of batter floats in cold water.
Beat in enough of the remaining broth to give the batter a soft, cake-batter consistency that holds its shape on a spoon; adjust salt to taste.
For the lightest tamales, chill the batter for about an hour, then re-beat with a little more broth or water to restore the soft consistency.

Prepare the banana leaves: trim off the tough side ribs and cut the leaves into twenty 12-inch unbroken segments. Soften them by steaming briefly or passing them over an open flame until pliable and glossy.

Set up a steamer (a collapsible vegetable steamer in a deep pot, a tamale steamer, or a rack set on cups in a large kettle works), lining the rack with leftover banana leaf scraps to protect the tamales and add flavor.

Form the tamales: lay a banana leaf square shiny-side up and spread about 1/3 cup batter into an 8x4-inch rectangle. Spoon 2 tablespoons filling over the left side of the batter, then fold the leaf to enclose the filling, folding in the top and bottom to make a tight package, and tie with string or a banana-leaf strip.

Arrange the tamales in the steamer (no more than two layers deep), cover with banana leaf scraps, put the lid on, and steam over steady medium heat for about 1.5 hours, topping up with boiling water as needed.

The tamales are done when the leaf peels away from the masa easily. Let them firm up off the heat for a few minutes; for the best texture, cool completely and re-steam about 15 minutes before serving.

Add the tomatoes, onion, and half the parsley and basil; simmer on low until reduced by half, about 1 hour, then stir in half the remaining herbs, season with salt, and discard the onion.

Set up a breading station: flour in one bowl, beaten eggs with 1 teaspoon salt in a second, and the panko mixed with the remaining 2 teaspoons oregano and 1/4 cup parmesan in a third. Dredge each eggplant slice in flour, dip in egg, then coat in the seasoned breadcrumbs.
Heat the vegetable oil to 375°F in a large skillet. Fry the breaded eggplant in small batches, about 2 1/2 minutes per side, until golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels and salt immediately.

Preheat the oven to 375°F. In a 9x13-inch baking dish, layer a quarter of the sauce, a third of the eggplant, another quarter of the sauce, and a third each of the mozzarella and remaining parmesan. Repeat for two more layers, saving 1/4 cup parmesan for the top.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes, then uncover and bake until golden and bubbling, about 20 more minutes. Let rest 15 minutes, top with the remaining parsley, basil, and parmesan, and serve.

ingredients.rawText: 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar (or balsamic glaze - thicker!)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil or a silicone mat.
Trim the dry outer leaves and stem ends off the brussels sprouts, then slice each one lengthwise.
Toss the sprouts in a large bowl with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the salt, and pepper until well coated.
Spread on the baking sheet and roast until tender and caramelized, about 20 minutes.
Return the roasted sprouts to the bowl, add the remaining tablespoon of olive oil, the balsamic vinegar, and honey, and toss to coat. Taste and add more salt if needed, then serve.

R0236.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Kevin Is Cooking's Balsamic Glazed Roasted Brussels Sprouts recipe, 2026-08-30 -- exact match on quantities and method; instructions paraphrased. Note: use frozen sprouts thawed and drained, roasting 40 minutes instead of 20.

ingredients.rawText: 2 lamb racks, about 1 1/2 pounds each, preferably frenched
ingredients.item: lamb racks, about 1.5 lbs each, preferably frenched

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 to 2 pounds small, round potatoes, scrubbed and left whole
ingredients.item: small round potatoes, scrubbed and left whole

ingredients.rawText: 2 tablespoons roughly chopped parsley, for garnish

instructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Season the lamb generously with salt and pepper. Mix the mustard, garlic, and anchovy together (mashing them in a mortar for a smoother paste), then stir in 3 tablespoons olive oil and rub it all over the lamb; set aside.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until a knife tip meets no resistance, 10-15 minutes. Drain, transfer to a roasting pan in a single layer, and let cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Gently crush the potatoes to crack them open and flatten slightly, then sprinkle with salt and drizzle with about 2 tablespoons olive oil, tossing to coat.

Lay the lamb racks on top of the potatoes, bones curving down, and scatter the rosemary over everything. Roast uncovered until a thermometer reads 125°F for medium-rare (or 135°F for medium), about 20 minutes.
Move the lamb to a cutting board, tent with foil, and let rest. Put the potatoes back in the oven for another 10-15 minutes until nicely crisped.
Slice the racks between the bones into chops, then serve with the potatoes, sprinkled with parsley.

ingredients.rawText: 3 medium cloves garlic (1/2 ounce; 15g) minced (about 1 tablespoon)
2 tablespoons (8g) finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves
1 tablespoon (6g) finely grated lemon zest (from 1 lemon)
2 tablespoons (18g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt (use half as much by volume, or the same weight, for table salt)
One 6- to 8-pound boneless leg of lamb, butterflied to even 1-inch thickness and trimmed of excess fat
ingredients.item: 6-8 lb boneless leg of lamb, butterflied to even 1-inch thickness, trimmed

instructions.text: Set an oven rack in the lower third and preheat to 275°F. Warm the olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat until shimmering, about 3 minutes.

Add the garlic, shallot, anchovies, rosemary, lemon zest, and red pepper flakes, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the shallot and garlic soften, 3-5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the salt and pepper.

Rub half the mixture inside the butterflied lamb leg, then roll it up and tie securely with butcher's twine at 1-inch intervals. Rub the rest of the mixture over the outside. Cook right away, or refrigerate uncovered up to 12 hours for deeper flavor.

When ready to cook, set the lamb fat-side up on a wire rack over a foil-lined baking sheet and roast until an instant-read thermometer reads 125-130°F for medium-rare (or 130-135°F for medium), about 2.5-3 hours. Let rest uncovered for 40 minutes.
Raise the oven to 500°F. Return the lamb to the oven and roast until the exterior is deeply browned and crisp, about 15 minutes. Let rest 5 more minutes.
Remove the twine, slice into 1/4-inch slices, and serve.

ingredients.item: dark brown sugar or Mexican brown sugar

ingredients.rawText: 2 pounds inside skirt steak, cut into 3 equal pieces
ingredients.item: inside skirt steak, cut into 3 equal pieces

instructions.text: Get charcoal (natural chunk if possible) going until it's covered in grey ash.

Blend the oil, soy sauce, scallions, garlic, lime juice, red pepper flakes, cumin, and brown sugar into a marinade. Put the skirt steak pieces in a large zip-top bag, pour in the marinade, and press out the air before sealing. Marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Remove the steak from the bag and pat dry. Blow any ash off the coals with a hair dryer.
Lay the steaks directly on the clean hot coals and cook for 1 minute per side.
Wrap the cooked meat in a double layer of foil and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Unwrap, reserving the foil and its juices, and slice the meat thinly against the grain. Return the slices to the foil and toss with the juices. Serve with grilled peppers and onions, if you like.

ingredients.rawText: 1 can (12 oz. / 340 g) Spam, sliced into 8 pieces
4 cups cooked sushi rice (or regular cooked white rice)
ingredients.item: cooked sushi rice (or regular cooked short-grain white rice)

ingredients.rawText: 3 sheets roasted seaweed nori, cut into 8 strips about 2" (5 cm) wide and 9" (23 cm) long
ingredients.item: roasted nori, cut into 8 strips (2in x 9in)

instructions.text: Have your steamed or sushi rice ready ahead of time.
Heat a large nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over medium heat. Cook the Spam slices until browned and crisp on the bottom, 2-3 minutes, then flip and brown the other side the same way.

Whisk the water and soy sauce together, sprinkle the sugar evenly over the Spam, then pour in the soy mixture. Let it simmer, flipping once, until the liquid is nearly absorbed and the sugar caramelizes, 3-4 minutes. Move the Spam to a plate to cool.

To assemble, lay one Spam slice crosswise on the bottom of a nori strip. Wet your hands, scoop 1/2 cup of rice, and press it into a ball, then shape it against the Spam into a rectangle about the same size as the slice.

Set the rice on top of the Spam, then roll the nori strip up and around the stack, sealing the end with a dab of water. Set the musubi seam-side down and repeat with the remaining Spam, rice, and nori.
Serve at room temperature, or store airtight in the fridge and reheat briefly in the microwave before serving.

ingredients.rawText: 1 cup small thin square-size coconut slices (thengakothu, optional)
ingredients.item: small thin square-size coconut slices (thengakothu), optional
salt, to taste, for the masala

instructions.text: Marinate the cleaned chicken pieces with salt, pepper powder, turmeric powder, and lemon juice. Set aside for 30 minutes.

Crush the whole black pepper (adjust the amount to your spice tolerance). Thinly slice the onions and green chillies, and grind the ginger and garlic into a fine paste. If using, thinly slice the coconut into small square pieces.
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in a pan and fry the coconut pieces until golden brown, then set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a kadai. Add the onions and curry leaves and sauté well - a pinch of salt helps the onions cook faster.
Once the onions are browned, add the ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté until the aromatics release their fragrance.
Add the garam masala, fennel powder, and crushed black pepper, and sauté briefly.
Add the marinated chicken and stir until well coated with the masala. Do not add water.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, then uncover and continue cooking until the released water evaporates. Stir in the fried coconut pieces.
Add 2-3 teaspoons of oil and sauté until well roasted. For extra tang, stir in the vinegar at the end if desired. Best served with rice.

R0414.title: Kerala Style Pepper Chicken (Nadan Kurumulaku Kozhi)

ingredients.rawText: 4 to 5 pounds chuck roast, cut into large 4-inch chunks
ingredients.item: chuck roast, cut into large chunks

ingredients.rawText: 12 guajillo chiles, rinsed, stemmed, and seeded (about 2.5 oz)
5 ancho chiles, rinsed, stemmed, and seeded (about 2 oz)
5 arbol chiles, rinsed and stemmed (about 0.1 oz)
2 cups shredded cheese (Oaxaca, Chihuahua, Asadero, Monterey Jack, or mozzarella)

instructions.text: Season the chunks of chuck roast all over with the salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the meat in batches on all sides, then set the seared meat aside in the pot.

While the meat browns, simmer the guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles with the tomatoes, onion half, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a separate pot of water for about 10 minutes, covered, until softened.

Lift the softened chiles and aromatics into a blender along with a cup of the chile-cooking liquid, the beef broth, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, and cloves. Blend until completely smooth, working in batches if needed.
Strain the blended sauce through a fine-mesh strainer directly into the pot with the seared meat, discarding the solids left behind.
Stir the meat into the chile sauce, bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer, cover, and cook for roughly 3 to 3 1/2 hours until the meat falls apart easily.
Lift the meat out and shred it with two forks. Let the braising liquid (consomme) sit for about 10 minutes so the fat rises to the top.
Dip a corn tortilla lightly on both sides into that top fat layer and lay it in a hot skillet. Pile shredded cheese and shredded meat over one half.
Fold the tortilla over and pan-fry about a minute per side until the cheese melts and the outside turns crisp and browned; repeat for the remaining tacos.
Tuck diced onion and cilantro into each taco and plate them with lime wedges and a small bowl of the consomme for dipping.

ingredients.rawText: 1 tsp sea salt, plus a pinch
2 tbsp chopped fennel fronds, more for garnish

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Pat the pork chops dry and use a sharp paring knife to cut a deep pocket into the fatty edge of each chop. Season all over with 1 teaspoon of salt, including inside the pockets.
Finely grate the lemon zest into a small bowl, then halve the lemon for juicing later.

Mash the garlic with a pinch of salt into a paste (using a mortar and pestle or the flat of a knife). Stir it into the lemon zest along with the rosemary, red pepper flakes, fennel seeds, 2 tablespoons of the fennel fronds, and 1 tablespoon of the olive oil.
Divide the filling between the pork chops, packing it into the pockets and rubbing the rest over the outside.

Heat the remaining tablespoon of olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over high heat. Sear the chops on one side for about 5 minutes until golden brown, flip and cook for 1 more minute, then transfer the skillet to the oven.
Roast until just cooked through, 5-10 minutes. Remove, tent with foil, and let rest for 10 minutes. Garnish with the remaining fennel fronds and a squeeze of lemon juice before serving.

instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the sifted flour, brown sugar, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, stir together the buttermilk, oil, vanilla, and grated carrot.
Fold the dry mixture into the wet ingredients until just combined.
Mix in the chopped almonds and raisins.
Pour the batter into a 10-ounce microwave-safe mug and microwave on high for about 2 to 2 1/2 minutes, then let it rest for another 30 seconds before checking it's set.
Serve the cake warm, plain or drizzled with honey or chocolate syrup.

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 to 2 tsp biryani masala (or chicken masala)
2 tbsp hot milk, soaked with saffron (optional)

instructions.text: Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear, then soak it for 30 minutes and drain.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the bay leaf and shahi jeera (whole spices can be tied in a muslin cloth if you'd rather not bite into them).
Salt the boiling water, add the drained rice, and parboil it until about 90% cooked and still firm at the center, then drain to a colander.
Meanwhile, fry the sliced onions in hot oil until golden and crisp; set aside a portion of the fried onions for layering later.
In the same pot, briefly saute the bay leaf, star anise, shahi jeera, cardamom, and cloves, then stir in the ginger garlic paste and cook until the raw smell fades.

Add the chicken and cook until it turns pale, then season with salt, biryani masala, chili powder, turmeric, and the slit green chilies; cook covered on low for a few minutes so the chicken releases moisture.
Stir in the yogurt, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender and the gravy thickens with the oil separating; adjust salt and stir in chopped mint and coriander.
Spread the parboiled rice evenly over the chicken gravy. Scatter the reserved fried onions, more mint and coriander, and, if using, the saffron milk, ghee, and kewra water.
Seal the pot tightly with foil or a moist cloth and a heavy lid to trap the steam, then set it over a hot griddle or tawa and cook on medium heat for about 12 to 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, still covered, for at least 20 minutes before opening and gently fluffing the layers together to serve.

R0269.note: The original scan for this card was too degraded/garbled to transcribe or verify against a specific source, though it retained partial content about par-boiling rice with whole spices and dum-style layering. This is a comparable, well-regarded restaurant-style Chicken Dum Biryani recipe from Swasthi's Recipes (Swasthi Shreekanth), used as a stand-in for the archived card's content, 2026-09-01; instructions paraphrased.

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a medium pot over medium-high heat, then add the ginger and garlic and cook briefly, about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Pour in the stock, add the rice and salt, and bring to a boil, stirring once.
Cover the pot, reduce the heat to low, and let the rice cook for about 12 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and let it rest, still covered, for 10 minutes so the rice finishes steaming and absorbs the remaining liquid.
Fluff the rice and scatter chopped green onions over the top before serving.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 kg chicken, skinless, preferably bone-in thighs and drumsticks
1 large onion, or 1/3 cup store-bought fried onions
1/4 tsp saffron strands, soaked in 3 tbsp hot milk
1 to 1 1/2 tsp biryani masala powder (or garam masala)

instructions.text: Slice the onion thin and separate the layers, then fry in hot oil or ghee, stirring often, until deep golden brown; remove and set aside, and reserve the flavored oil for the marinade.
Whisk together the yogurt, salt, turmeric, chili powder, biryani masala, cardamom powder, green chili, ginger garlic paste, and lemon juice in a large bowl; taste and adjust seasoning.
Add the chicken to the marinade, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight, for the most tender result.
Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes, then drain.

Bring water to a boil with a teaspoon of oil, salt, and the whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, star anise, and optional black cardamom, mace, and caraway); let it boil a few minutes to release the aroma.
Add the drained rice and cook until about three-quarters done, with a slight bite still in the center, then drain to a colander.
Transfer the marinated chicken to a heavy-bottomed pot, mix in oil, half the fried onions, and some of the mint and coriander, and spread it into an even layer.
Spread the parboiled rice evenly over the chicken. Scatter more fried onions, mint, and coriander, a pinch more biryani masala, the saffron milk, and finish with the ghee on top.
Seal the pot tightly with foil or a moist cloth and a heavy lid to trap the steam for the dum process.

Set the pot over a hot griddle or tawa on medium-high heat for 15 to 20 minutes, then lower the heat to a bare simmer for another 15 minutes; alternatively, dum-bake in a 390F (200C) oven for 30 to 40 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, covered, for 20 to 30 minutes before opening the seal, gently fluffing the layers, and garnishing with fresh coriander to serve.

R0268.title: Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani Recipe

ingredients.rawText: 1 block or 14 ounce tofu, extra firm
1 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari for gluten free)
ingredients.item: soy sauce (or tamari for gluten free), for the tofu
corn starch, for coating the tofu

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 tbsp sriracha or any Asian hot sauce
ingredients.item: sriracha or any Asian hot sauce

ingredients.rawText: 2 tbsp brown sugar (may use honey or agave)
1 tsp ginger, grated or finely minced
1 tsp garlic, grated or finely minced
1/2 tsp black pepper powder, or less

instructions.text: Wrap the tofu block in kitchen paper or a clean towel and set it in a colander in the sink. Weigh it down with something heavy for 20-30 minutes to press out the excess liquid (or use a tofu press).

Cut the pressed tofu into 1-inch cubes. Toss gently in a bowl with the 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, then sprinkle over the 1 tablespoon of corn starch and mix gently to coat - an uneven coating is fine.

Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 3-4 minutes. Line the basket with air fryer parchment (or grease it well) and arrange the tofu cubes with space between them, in batches if needed, misting lightly with cooking oil.
Air fry at 400°F for 15-16 minutes, flipping the cubes around the 7-8 minute mark, until crispy outside and soft inside. Don't over-fry or the tofu will dry out. Set aside.

While the tofu air fries, make the sauce: whisk the ginger, garlic, 3 tablespoons soy sauce, sriracha, sesame oil, black pepper, 2 tablespoons corn starch, and the water together in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.

Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring to prevent the corn starch from clumping, then turn off the heat. Season with salt and adjust heat/sweetness to taste - it will thicken further as it sits.
Add the air-fried tofu to the sauce and mix gently to coat. Sprinkle with the toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions, and serve warm with rice on the side.

ingredients.rawText: 3 lbs. beef chuck roast, cut into 1 1/2 - 2" chunks and trimmed of excess fat
ingredients.item: beef chuck roast, cut into chunks

ingredients.rawText: 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into 1 1/2" chunks
3 parsnips, peeled and cut into 1" chunks

instructions.text: Set the Instant Pot to Saute and heat 1 tablespoon of the oil. Brown the beef chunks in two batches so they sear rather than steam, then set the meat aside on a plate.
In the same pot, soften the chopped onion for a few minutes, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste briefly.

Pour in the Guinness and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, then return the browned beef and any juices to the pot along with the bay leaf and thyme.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 30 minutes, then quick-release. Discard the bay leaf and thyme stems.
Add the carrots, celery and parsnips, reseal, and pressure cook on high for another 5 minutes, then quick-release again.
Mix the cornstarch with a couple tablespoons of water and stir it into the stew on the Saute setting until the gravy thickens, about 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper before serving.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 kg (1.1 lbs) boneless chicken, cut into 1-inch pieces (or 3/4 kg bone-in chicken, curry-cut)
1 1/4 cup (300 g) tomato puree (about 2 medium tomatoes, pureed)
1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder (up to 1 teaspoon for more heat)
1/2 to 1 teaspoon garam masala, to taste
3 tablespoons heavy cream or yogurt (or 10 cashews, pureed)
ingredients.item: heavy cream or yogurt (or cashew puree)

ingredients.rawText: 1 tablespoon butter or ghee (for stir-frying vegetables)
1/2 cup onions, cubed and layers separated (optional)
1 dried Kashmiri red chili (for kadai masala)
2 to 3 black peppercorns, or 1/8 teaspoon crushed pepper (for kadai masala)

instructions.text: Toast the coriander seeds and dried red chili in a dry pan for a couple of minutes, then add the fennel seeds, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom and toast until fragrant. Cool and grind to a fine powder to make the kadai masala.
Heat oil or ghee in a kadai/wok. Add cumin seeds and the broken red chili, then add the chopped onions and cook until golden, about 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste for about a minute, then add the chicken and sauté for 3-4 minutes until it turns pale.
Lower the heat and mix in the turmeric, chili powder, salt and the ground kadai masala, then pour in the tomato puree. Cook until the puree thickens and loses its raw smell, about 3-4 minutes.
Partially cover and continue cooking until the chicken is tender and the gravy has thickened.

Meanwhile, in a separate pan, melt the butter and stir-fry the cubed onions and capsicum on high heat for a couple of minutes so they stay crunchy but slightly charred, then fold them into the chicken along with the kasuri methi.
Stir in the cream, yogurt or cashew paste (tempered first with a little of the hot gravy so it doesn't split), and simmer for 2-3 minutes without overcooking the peppers.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves (or ginger juliennes and slit green chili) and serve with flatbread or rice.

ingredients.rawText: 2 lbs (1 kg) beef stew meat or beef chuck, cut into 2-inch pieces
ingredients.item: beef stew meat or chuck, cut into pieces

ingredients.rawText: 1 tablespoon Kashmiri chili powder, or to taste
1 teaspoon fennel powder, preferably freshly ground
1/2 cup coconut slices, fresh or frozen
2 green chilies (serrano or similar), or to taste

instructions.text: Combine the beef with the chili powder, coriander powder, fennel powder, garam masala, pepper, salt, garlic, ginger, shallots, curry leaves and water in a pressure cooker (or Instant Pot) and cook at high pressure for about 15 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally.
Lift the cooked beef out of the pot with a slotted spoon and set it aside, keeping the flavorful cooking liquid for later.

Heat coconut oil in a heavy skillet, briefly fry the coconut slices, then add turmeric and salt and cook until lightly browned. Add the sliced onions, green chilies, ginger and garlic and cook until the onions turn golden.
Add the cooked beef and curry leaves and saute for a few minutes until the meat starts to catch on the bottom of the pan.
Add the reserved cooking liquid a quarter cup at a time, scraping up the browned bits and letting it reduce almost completely before adding more, repeating until most of the liquid is used.
Once the beef is glossy, very dark and coated in a thick, dry masala with no pooled liquid remaining, stir in the last bit of fennel powder, garam masala and black pepper and serve.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 kg (500 g) chicken, bone-in cut preferred (or boneless thighs/drumsticks)
1/4 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri or byadgi, less spicy kind), for marinade
1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon crushed black pepper, for marinade
3/4 cup onions, chopped or sliced finely (about 1 large)
1/4 teaspoon cumin seeds (optional, for spice paste)
2 to 4 dried red chilies (for spice paste)
1 dried red chili, broken, for tempering
3 to 4 pearl onions or shallots, thinly sliced, for tempering

instructions.text: Rub the chicken with chili powder, salt, turmeric, pepper, garam masala and lemon juice and set aside to marinate while you prepare the rest.

Dry-roast the coriander seeds, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, peppercorns and dried chilies until fragrant, then separately roast the fennel and cumin. Grind everything together with a little water into a smooth spice paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and cook the onions until golden. Add the ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then stir in the tomatoes if using and cook until they break down.
Add the marinated chicken and sear on high heat for a few minutes until it turns white, then stir in the ground spice paste.
Cover and cook on low heat until the chicken is tender and cooked through, adding a splash of hot water only if the pan looks too dry.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer uncovered for about 5 minutes until the curry thickens slightly. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.

ingredients.rawText: 3 cups mixed dried fruits (sultanas, seedless raisins, currants, candied orange and lemon peel)

1 cup + 2 tablespoons sugar, for the batter
250 g unsalted butter, at room temperature
A small piece of cinnamon, for spice powder
A small piece of nutmeg, for spice powder

instructions.text: Soak the mixed dried fruit in rum or brandy in a covered jar for at least a week (traditionally much longer), shaking the jar occasionally.

To make the caramel, melt the sugar with a tablespoon of water over heat until it turns a dark brown color, then carefully stir in the warm water (it will spatter) and simmer a few more minutes before letting it cool completely.
Grind the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and nutmeg with a pinch of sugar into a fine spice powder.

Preheat the oven to 180C (350F). Drain the soaked fruit, reserving a few tablespoons of the soaking liquid, and toss the drained fruit in a little flour so it doesn't sink in the batter. Sift together the flour, baking powder and baking soda.

Whip the egg whites to soft peaks and set aside. Beat the egg yolks with the softened butter until smooth, then gradually beat in the sugar until fluffy. Mix in the vanilla, the cooled caramel and the spice powder.
Fold in the sifted dry ingredients in two additions, then stir in the jam.
Gently fold the beaten egg whites into the batter in two parts until no streaks remain, then fold in the floured soaked fruit along with the reserved soaking liquid.
Pour the batter into a greased, lined cake tin and bake for about 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool before slicing.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease an 8-inch square or 9-inch round cake pan and line it with parchment paper for easy removal.

Make the crumbs: whisk the melted butter, brown sugar, granulated sugar, cinnamon, and salt together until evenly combined. Stir in the flour until it disappears into a very thick mixture. Press it evenly into the bottom of the bowl and set aside.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350F.

Set the caramel-lined cake pan inside a larger roasting pan, then pour the custard mixture over the hardened caramel.

Remove the cake pan from the water bath, cool it to room temperature on a rack, then chill it in the refrigerator if you prefer it cold.
To unmold, run a thin knife around the edge, place a serving plate upside down over the pan, and flip both together so the caramel sauce pours over the custard. Slice and serve.

If you are not making the blistered serranos, deglaze the pan with the lime juice, season the onions with salt, and set aside. If you are making the blistered serranos, just transfer the onions to a plate without deglazing.

If making the blistered serranos: cut each chile lengthwise from just below the stem to the tip, then give it a quarter turn and make a second similar cut, so each chile ends up in four long pieces still held together at the stem.

Add another tablespoon of lard and the cut chiles to the pan and cook, about 5 minutes, until blistered all over (make sure the kitchen is well ventilated). Deglaze with lime juice, season with salt, and transfer to a plate.

When it's very hot and just starting to smoke, lay the meat in a single layer (working in two batches if needed). Sear about 1 1/2 minutes per side until browned, then transfer to a cutting board, tenting with foil if searing in batches.

instructions.text: Cut the chicken into small cubes, wash it with a little turmeric powder, then drain and set aside.

Heat a pan until hot, then lower the flame and dry-roast the peppercorns, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, and fennel seeds, stirring often, until they darken slightly and become fragrant. Let cool, then grind to a coarse powder.
Marinate the chicken with the ground roasted spices along with the chilli flakes, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, vinegar or lemon juice, and salt. Refrigerate for about 30 minutes to an hour.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a pan and fry the coconut slices until light brown, then remove and drain on a paper towel.

In the same pan, add the remaining oil, the finely sliced shallots/onions, and the green chilies. Saute until translucent and light brown, then add the curry leaves and saute for a couple more minutes.
Add the marinated chicken, combine well, and fry for about 5 minutes. Cover and cook until the chicken is fully cooked through, about 20-25 minutes.
Uncover, add the tomato sauce or puree, and roast over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally to prevent burning, until it turns dark brown, about 15-20 minutes.
Once the chicken has dried out and turned dark brown, add the fried coconut slices and mix well. The dish should be dry with no gravy - if any water remains, keep roasting until it evaporates.
Serve hot with parotta, rice, appam, kappa, or any Indian bread.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a pan over low heat. Add the cumin seeds followed by the black pepper and stir about a minute. Add the coconut and keep stirring a couple of minutes.
Add the turmeric powder and saute a couple of minutes, then the coriander powder and saute about a minute, then the chili powder and stir until the raw smell is gone.
Turn off the heat, let the mixture cool slightly, then grind it with enough water to a fine masala paste.
In a separate pan, heat oil and splutter the mustard seeds, then add cumin seeds and the chopped onions. Saute until the onions turn translucent.
Add the ginger garlic paste and curry leaves and saute a couple of minutes, then add turmeric powder and saute until its raw smell is gone.
Puree the tomatoes (boil briefly, peel, and blend), then add the tomato puree and salt. Turn the heat to medium, cover, and cook until the oil separates.
Stir in the ground masala paste with a little water and the garam masala. Mix well, cover, and cook for about 15-20 minutes over medium heat until the gravy thickens.
In another pan, heat a little oil, add the boiled eggs, and stir for about a minute over medium heat. Season with salt and chili powder.
Add the seasoned eggs and the vinegar to the simmering gravy, stirring gently to coat the eggs without breaking them. Simmer a few minutes until the curry reaches the desired consistency.
Check the seasoning, adjust salt and spice as needed, then switch off the heat and serve hot with rice or roti.

instructions.text: Dry roast the coriander seeds, fennel seeds, peppercorns, cloves, and cardamom seeds in a pan over low heat for about 3 minutes, then let them cool and grind into a masala powder.

Lower the heat, add the ginger garlic paste, and fry for 2 minutes, then stir in the tomato puree and continue cooking over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until the oil separates.

instructions.text: Whisk the semolina, rice flour, and all-purpose flour together, gradually adding water while stirring to avoid lumps, until the batter has a thin, pourable consistency similar to buttermilk.
Mix in the cumin seeds, salt, asafoetida, cilantro, and chopped green chili. Let the batter rest for about 30 minutes.
Heat a flat griddle over medium-high heat. Check readiness by flicking on a few drops of water; they should sizzle. Wipe the surface with a little oil.

Pour the batter from a height of about 3 to 4 inches, starting at the outer edge and spiraling toward the center until the griddle is covered. Avoid spreading it with a spatula so the batter keeps its lacy, holey texture.
Drizzle about a teaspoon of oil around the edges of the dosa.
Cook over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until the underside turns golden brown, then flip with a spatula.
Cook the second side for roughly a minute more, until lightly colored.
Remove from the griddle and serve immediately while thin and crisp, traditionally alongside coconut chutney and sambar.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350F.
Melt the butter in a small bowl in the microwave and set aside.
In a large bowl, stir together the sugar and yogurt. Mix in the semolina, baking powder, and milk, then stir in the melted butter and let the batter sit briefly so the butter is absorbed.
Pour the batter into a lightly greased 9-inch round cake pan and bake for about 40-45 minutes, until set. Broil briefly at the end if the top needs more color, watching closely so it doesn't burn.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
A day (or up to two days) ahead, soak the chopped dry fruits, sultanas, raisins, and nuts in the dark rum until they fully absorb it.
Line two baking pans with parchment paper and butter the sides and bottom. Set aside.

Make the caramel: heat the sugar in a saucepan over low heat, stirring as it crystallizes and then slowly melts, until it turns a deep dark color. Remove from the heat, carefully stir in the water, and return to low heat until the sugar dissolves again. Set aside to cool.
Toss the soaked dry fruit mixture with the 2 tablespoons of flour to coat. Set aside.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and spice powders. Set aside.
Beat the butter, sugar, and vanilla together with an electric beater until creamy.
Add 2 of the eggs and beat until creamy, then add the remaining 3 eggs and beat again until creamy.
Fold in the remaining flour mixture along with the cooled caramel.
Gently fold in the flour-tossed dry fruit mixture.
Divide the batter between the prepared pans and bake for 40-45 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool completely, then invert the pans and peel off the parchment paper.
Slice and serve.

instructions.text: Toast the panko first: heat a dry skillet over medium heat, add the panko, and toast, stirring frequently, for 2-4 minutes until golden and fragrant. Remove from the heat and let cool - this keeps the crust from turning soggy and adds texture.

Make the herb crust: in a medium bowl, combine the toasted panko, chopped rosemary, thyme, parsley, pressed garlic, olive oil, Parmesan (if using), salt, and pepper. Mix until it holds together loosely like damp sand, adding a touch more olive oil if it feels too dry.
Prepare and sear the lamb: let the racks sit out for 30-45 minutes to come to room temperature, then pat them very dry and season generously on all sides with kosher salt and black pepper.

Heat 1-2 tablespoons of high-smoke-point oil in a large oven-safe skillet (cast iron works well) over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the racks fat-side down first for 3-5 minutes until well browned, then flip and sear the remaining sides for 2-3 minutes total. Work in batches if needed, then remove from the heat.

Apply the crust: brush a thin, even layer of Dijon mustard over the meaty side and lightly onto the sides of each seared rack - this acts as the glue for the crust. Press the herb-panko mixture firmly onto the mustard-coated areas so it adheres well.

Roast the lamb: preheat (or have ready) an oven at 425°F (220°C). Transfer the crusted racks, still in the oven-safe skillet (or onto a baking sheet), and roast for 12-20 minutes depending on size and desired doneness, starting to check the internal temperature at the 12-minute mark. Aim for 125-130°F (52-54°C) for medium-rare, or 135-140°F (57-60°C) for medium, measured in the thickest part of the meat away from the bone. The crust should be golden and crisp.

Rest and serve: remove from the oven, tent loosely with foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes (the internal temperature will rise a few more degrees as it rests). Slice between the bones into individual or double chops and serve immediately.

instructions.text: Make the oat crumble topping: whisk the flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt together in a medium bowl. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or a silicone mat and set aside. Position a rack in the lower third of the oven and preheat to 425F.

Transfer the dough to the pie dish, letting it settle into the bottom, and press it firmly into the base and up the sides. Trim the overhang to about half an inch, tuck it under itself for a thick edge, and crimp decoratively. Chill the lined shell in the freezer while you prepare the filling.
Make the filling by tossing the sliced apples with the brown sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, cider vinegar, and salt in a large bowl until evenly coated.

Scrape about a quarter of the apple mixture into the chilled crust and arrange the slices to fill gaps, then add the rest of the filling and juices, mounding and pressing it toward the center. Scatter the chilled butter pieces over the top, then break up and sprinkle the oat crumble evenly over the apples.

Set the pie on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes at 425F, then lower the oven to 350F and continue baking until the crust is golden and the filling is visibly bubbling, roughly another 40 to 75 minutes. Tent loosely with foil if the crumble browns too quickly.

instructions.text: Rinse the eggplant and pat it dry, then rub oil all over the skin. Roast it directly over an open flame (or on a grill or in the oven), turning every 2 to 3 minutes so it cooks evenly and picks up a smoky flavor. You can tuck a few garlic cloves into the flesh before roasting.

instructions.text: Remove the stems and seeds from the dried chiles. Toast them in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, just until fragrant, taking care not to scorch them. Soak the toasted chiles in a bowl of hot water for 15-20 minutes.
Blend the softened chiles with the onion, garlic, tomatoes, vinegar, oregano, cumin, paprika, cloves, black pepper, and about 1 cup of the beef broth until smooth.
Season the beef generously with salt. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned on all sides, so it browns rather than steams.

Pour the chile sauce over the seared beef, then add the remaining beef broth, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer, cover, and cook for 3 to 3.5 hours, until the beef is very tender and shreds easily (alternatively, a slow cooker on low for 8 hours or an Instant Pot for 60-70 minutes with natural release both work).

Lift the beef out of the pot and shred it with two forks. Skim some of the red fat that has risen to the top of the broth and reserve it in a small bowl; this consomme fat is what crisps and flavors the tortillas.

Dip each corn tortilla in the reserved fat, then lay it on a hot griddle or skillet. Fill one half with shredded beef and shredded cheese, fold the tortilla over, and fry on both sides until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Skim the broth of any remaining fat and warm it as a dipping consomme.
Serve the crispy tacos hot with the warm consomme for dipping, alongside chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges, and salsa or hot sauce.

Stir in the turmeric and chopped spinach, cover with a lid, and cook over medium flame for a few minutes.

R0054.title: Aloo Palak (Spinach and Potatoes)

ingredients.rawText: 250 gms unsalted butter (1 cup + 2 tbsp, approx @ room temp)
A small piece cinnamon (for spice powder)
A small piece nutmeg (for spice powder)

instructions.text: Soak the fruits: use a combination of sultanas, seedless raisins, currants and candied orange and lemon peel (or dried fruits of choice, chopped small if using dates/apricots). Soak in the rum/brandy for a minimum of 1 week (up to 1.5 months), shaking the jar occasionally.

Make the caramel: combine sugar and 1 tablespoon water in a saucepan. Heat and let the sugar melt until dark brown. Remove from heat and carefully add the warm water (it will splash). Return to heat and boil 3-4 more minutes. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Grind the spices with a pinch of sugar to a fine powder and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (355°F) for 10-15 minutes before baking.

Drain the soaked fruits, retaining 4 tablespoons of the liquor. Toss the drained fruits in 1-2 tablespoons of flour to prevent sinking. Sift the plain flour with baking powder and baking soda. Powder the sugar. Separate the egg yolks and whites; beat the whites to soft peaks and set aside.

Beat the egg yolks with the softened butter until a smooth paste forms. Gradually add the powdered sugar, beating after each addition. Once smooth, add vanilla essence, cooled caramel, and spice powder, and beat again.
Add the sifted flour in 2 batches, beating after each addition. Add jam and combine.
Fold in the beaten egg whites in 2 parts, combining until no white streaks remain. Fold in the soaked fruits and the 4 tablespoons of retained liquor.
Grease the baking dish and line with baking paper. Pour the batter into the prepared tins. Bake in the preheated oven for 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Alcohol-free version: soak the 3 cups of fruit in 1.5 cups of fresh orange juice overnight at room temperature instead of rum, then follow the rest of the recipe the same way.

R0060.title: Xmas Fruit Cake / Kerala Plum Cake

ingredients.item: white wine vinegar, for the brine
ginger garlic paste, for the marinade

ingredients.rawText: 4-5 green onions, chopped finely (whites reserved for cooking, greens for garnish)
1 mid-size bell pepper/capsicum, cut into triangles
ingredients.item: mid-size bell pepper, cut into triangles

ingredients.rawText: 1 mid-size onion, cut into quarter bulbs
ingredients.item: mid-size onion, cut into quarter bulbs

instructions.text: Stir the cold water, salt, sugar, and vinegar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Add the chicken to this brine and refrigerate for 1.5 to 2 hours.
Lift the chicken from the brine (leaving the liquid behind) and toss it with the ginger-garlic paste, black pepper, and 2 tablespoons of oil. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Add the flour, cornstarch, and baking powder to the marinated chicken and mix until evenly coated.
Heat oil in a pan until hot, testing the temperature with a small drop of batter.
Fry the chicken for about 10 minutes, until cooked through on the outside.
Let the chicken rest for 15 minutes, then fry a second time for about 5 minutes until deep golden brown. Remove and let rest again.
Stir the cornstarch into the 1/4 cup water to make the sauce thickener.
Heat oil in a skillet and stir-fry the white parts of the green onions with the ginger and garlic for 2-3 minutes.
Add the onion and bell pepper and stir-fry 2-3 minutes, then pour in the cornstarch slurry and cook until it starts to bubble and thicken.
Stir in the sambal/chili garlic paste, soy sauce, salt, sugar, and black pepper.
Turn off the heat and let the sauce cool for about 5 minutes, then add the twice-fried chicken and toss to coat evenly in the sauce.
Garnish with the reserved green onion tops and serve immediately while the chicken is still crisp.

R0332.title: Ultimate Crispy Chili Chicken

ingredients.rawText: 4 large chicken breasts, boneless and skinless
ingredients.item: large chicken breasts, boneless and skinless

ingredients.rawText: 2 cups panko breadcrumbs, gluten-free if needed
1/2 cup all-purpose flour, gluten-free if needed

instructions.text: Preheat the air fryer to 380F and lightly mist the basket with non-stick spray.

Cut each chicken breast in half lengthwise to make 8 thin cutlets. Place each piece between plastic wrap or in a zip-top bag and pound with a meat mallet or rolling pin, working from the center outward, until it's an even 1/4 inch thick.
Set up 3 shallow bowls: one with the flour and half of the seasonings, one with the whisked eggs, and one with the panko and the remaining seasonings.

Dredge each cutlet in the flour mixture to coat all sides, then dip in the egg, and finally press into the panko, pressing firmly with your palm on both sides so the crumbs adhere. Repeat with all the cutlets.
Arrange the cutlets in the air fryer basket in a single layer without overlapping, working in batches as needed.
Air fry at 380F for 6 minutes, flip with tongs, then raise the temperature to 400F and cook 2-3 more minutes, until golden, crispy, and the internal temperature reaches 165F.
Let the cutlets rest briefly, then serve with lemon wedges.

R0336.title: Unidentified Chicken Recipe (Pages 2-3)

Mix all the marinade ingredients together in a bowl.
Rub the marinade over the chicken, including inside the cavity.
Refrigerate and let the chicken marinate for 3 hours.
Preheat the oven to 400F.
Place the chicken in a roasting pan, cover with foil, and bake for 20 minutes.
