R0400.title: Whole Chicken Roast Kerala Style

ingredients.rawText: 4 medium potatoes, baked or boiled until just fork tender and cooled
ingredients.item: potatoes, baked or boiled until just fork tender and cooled

ingredients.rawText: 1 teaspoon coconut sugar or brown sugar
2 to 3 fresh green chilies, seeded and finely chopped
ingredients.item: fresh green chilies, seeded and finely chopped

ingredients.rawText: 1-inch piece fresh ginger, minced or grated
1 lb (450 g) fresh spinach, trimmed and roughly chopped
ingredients.item: fresh spinach, trimmed and roughly chopped

instructions.text: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small wedges. In a small bowl, stir together the ground coriander, garam masala, turmeric, cumin, asafetida, sugar, lemon juice, and water to make a spice paste.

Heat the ghee or oil in a large heavy-bottomed nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potato wedges and fry, stirring gently, until golden brown, about 10 to 15 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the mustard and cumin seeds to the pan. Fry until the mustard seeds turn grey and begin to pop, then stir in the chilies and ginger for another minute.
Add the spice paste and cook, stirring, for a few minutes until most of the water evaporates. Stir in the tomato and simmer about 5 minutes, until it thickens and the liquid evaporates.
Add the spinach in handfuls, letting each batch wilt slightly before adding more. Cover and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover, stir in the salt, and cook another 5 minutes, until most of the liquid released by the spinach has evaporated.
Lower the heat, gently fold the potato wedges back in, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve hot as a vegetable side dish. Makes 4 to 6 side servings.

R0435.note: Ingredients confirmed against Lisa Turner's Saag Aloo recipe on Lisa's Kitchen (foodandspice.com), which matches the archived OCR fragment for the instructions and second half of the ingredient list exactly (the archived scan was cut off before the potato/spice-paste portion of the ingredient list). R0435.title: Aloo Palak (Spinach and Potatoes)

ingredients.rawText: 1.5 cups poha (red or white beaten rice / flattened rice)
ingredients.item: poha, red or white flattened rice

instructions.text: Rinse the poha in water until it softens - it should lose its crunchiness and crush easily between your fingers.
Add the sugar, salt, and turmeric powder to the rinsed poha and mix gently.
Dry roast the peanuts in a pan until crunchy, then set aside.
Heat the oil in the same pan and crackle the mustard seeds.
Add the onions and saute until translucent.
Add the curry leaves and green chilies and saute for about half a minute.
Add the roasted peanuts and stir them in.
Add the seasoned poha and stir to combine.
Cover and steam the poha for 2-3 minutes over low heat, giving it a stir after about 1 to 1.5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the poha sit covered for 1-2 minutes.
Uncover and sprinkle with lemon juice, coriander leaves, and grated coconut.
Give it a gentle stir and serve the kanda poha hot with tea.

R0148.title: Kanda Poha (Onion Poha)

instructions.text: Rinse the karela in water first.
Slice the karela into thin rounds. You can lightly peel the skin first if you prefer.
Heat the oil in a frying pan or kadai.
Add the karela slices and saute on low-medium heat, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add all the dry spice powders and salt.
Stir and saute for 5-6 more minutes on low heat.
Finally, stir in the besan (gram flour) and saute for another 4-5 minutes, until its raw smell is gone.
Garnish the karela sabzi with coriander leaves.
Serve the karela stir-fry with dal-rice, kadhi-rice, or sambar-rice.

R0247.note: Ingredients and steps transcribed directly from the scanned card's own OCR text (Dassana Amit's karela sabzi/stir-fry recipe on vegrecipesofindia.com, same author/style as the archive's other 'dassana' cards like Kanda Poha and Kadai Mushroom), 2026-09-02; instructions paraphrased.
R0247.title: Karela Sabzi (Bitter Gourd Stir-Fry)

ingredients.rawText: about 1/2 cup water, or as needed

instructions.text: Rinse and clean the chicken, then let it drain in a strainer.
Heat coconut oil in a large pan or kadai. Add the sliced onions and slit green chilies, and saute over low-medium heat until the onions begin to turn brown.
Meanwhile, grind the ginger and garlic together into a paste and set aside.
Once the onions are nearly browned, stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook on low heat for about a minute.
Add one sliced tomato and saute on low heat for about 3 minutes. While that cooks, puree the remaining tomatoes.
Add the pureed tomatoes and saute for 6-7 minutes, until oil starts to separate at the sides of the pan.
Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala along with about 2 tablespoons of water. Mix well and cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Add the chicken and mix thoroughly; let it cook for about 7 minutes so the moisture releases and the chicken lightly fries, then continue for about 10 more minutes until it's half cooked.
Pour in about 1/2 cup water, cover, and cook on low heat until the chicken is fully cooked through.
Stir in the sugar and a handful of extra curry leaves, then serve hot with rice, roti, appam, or puttu.

R0130.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against nisahomey.blogspot.com (Nisa Homey), 2026-09-02 - the archived scan's blog prose (tomato-puree technique, 5 onions, Easter-recipe framing) matches this page closely; the archive had only a fragment of the ingredients list (chicken, onions) and no parsed instructions. R0130.title: Kerala Chicken Curry Recipe

instructions.text: Clean the fish and set it aside.
Soak the kudampuli (kukum star) in the hot water for about 15 minutes to soften it and pull out its sourness.
Crush or coarsely grind the ginger, garlic, and shallots together.
Heat the coconut oil in a clay pot or heavy-bottomed pan. Add the mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add the fenugreek seeds and let them sizzle briefly.
Add the crushed ginger, garlic, and shallots along with the curry leaves, and saute until the shallots turn golden.
Stir in the turmeric powder, chilli powder, and Kashmiri chilli powder, and saute briefly until fragrant, being careful not to let the spices burn.
Pour in the soaked kudampuli along with its soaking liquid and the salt. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Slide in the cleaned fish pieces, cover, and simmer gently, without stirring too much, until the fish is cooked through and the gravy has thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let the curry rest for a while before serving - like most Kerala fish curries, the flavor deepens once it has settled.

R0214.title: Kerala Fish Curry

ingredients.rawText: Chicken with bones - 1.1 lb / 1/2 kg, cut into medium size pieces
ingredients.item: chicken with bones, cut into medium pieces

ingredients.rawText: Freshly crushed whole black pepper powder (for marination) - 1/2 tsp
ingredients.item: freshly crushed whole black pepper powder, for marination

ingredients.rawText: Shallots / red small onion (kochu ulli) - 25-30 nos, or 1 large onion, finely sliced
Tomato - 2 medium sized, chopped and ground to a paste
Freshly ground black pepper powder - 2-2 1/2 tsp, or to taste
ingredients.item: freshly ground black pepper powder, or to taste

ingredients.rawText: Curry leaves - 2 sprigs, plus 1 extra sprig to finish
ingredients.item: curry leaves, plus 1 extra sprig to finish

ingredients.rawText: Coconut oil - 2 tbsp, plus 1 tbsp for finishing
ingredients.item: coconut oil, plus 1 tbsp for finishing

instructions.text: Clean and wash the chicken pieces with turmeric powder, then drain.
Marinate the chicken for 30 minutes to 1 hour with the marination ingredients (turmeric, crushed black pepper, lemon juice, salt), then set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon of coconut oil in a pan. Add a few curry leaves, then the crushed ginger and garlic, and saute for a couple of minutes. Add the finely chopped shallots (or onion) and green chillies, and saute over medium-low heat until translucent.

Add the coriander powder and turmeric powder, and saute for a minute. Add the ground tomato paste with a couple tablespoons of water, and cook until the tomatoes are well cooked and most of the water has evaporated.
Add the marinated chicken pieces, mix well so they're coated with the masala, adjust the salt, and cook covered for about 20 minutes without adding water.

Uncover and cook for another 10 minutes. Add the freshly crushed black pepper powder, garam masala, grated coconut, and the extra sprig of curry leaves. Combine well and cook on low flame, stirring occasionally, until the chicken pieces dry out and turn light brown, about 10 minutes.
Add the remaining tablespoon of coconut oil and dry-roast, uncovered, until nicely browned.
Once the chicken starts to fall off the bone and turns a dark brown color, remove from heat. Keep covered for 10-20 minutes to let the flavors settle.
Serve as a side dish with steamed rice, roti, appam, or any Indian bread.

R0165.title: Kerala Pepper Chicken Fry Recipe - Nadan Kurumulaku Kozhi Fry Recipe

ingredients.rawText: Cilantro, a few sprigs, finely chopped

ingredients.item: chilli powder (split between cooking and marinating)

ingredients.rawText: Dry Red chilli 5 nos (for kadai masala)
ingredients.item: dry red chilli, for the kadai masala
coriander seeds, for the kadai masala

ingredients.rawText: Pepper corns 1/2 tsp or less (for kadai masala)

ingredients.item: fennel seeds, for the kadai masala
cumin seeds, for the kadai masala

ingredients.rawText: Kasoori Methi/Dry Methi leaves 1/2 tsp (for kadai masala)
ingredients.item: kasoori methi (dry fenugreek leaves), for the kadai masala

instructions.text: Wash the chicken, drain, and marinate with the turmeric powder and half the chilli powder; set aside.
Heat a pan and dry roast the dry red chilli, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, cumin seeds, and peppercorns for a minute, then add the kasoori methi at the end and remove from heat.
Let the roasted spices cool, then grind them into a coarse kadai masala powder and set aside.
Heat the 1/2 teaspoon of oil in the same pan and stir-fry the diced capsicum for 1-2 minutes, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a wok, add the cumin seeds and let them splutter, then add the finely chopped onions and saute for 2-3 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste with a pinch of salt and saute until the raw smell disappears.
Add the chopped tomato and tomato puree and cook until the oil separates and the moisture dries up.
Stir in half of the ground kadai masala and fry for a minute.

Add the chicken, the remaining kadai masala, and the turmeric powder, and stir for 3-4 minutes. Add 1/2 to 3/4 cup water plus enough salt, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and cook for another 1-2 minutes, then stir in the sauteed capsicum.
Let it simmer for one more minute and turn off the heat. Garnish with finely chopped cilantro and ginger julienne before serving.

R0307.title: Kadai Chicken

ingredients.rawText: 400-450 gms chicken, cut into medium size pieces, bone-in
ingredients.item: chicken, cut into medium pieces, bone-in

instructions.text: Marinate the cleaned chicken pieces with salt, pepper powder, and lemon juice. Crush the whole black pepper (do not powder it).

Heat oil in a pan and add the sliced onion. Let it brown. Add the grated/crushed ginger and garlic, green chilli, and curry leaves. Cook until the raw smell goes away, about 3-4 minutes. Add the crushed pepper, turmeric powder, garam masala, fennel powder, and chicken/meat masala (if using). Mix well and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add the soya sauce and tomato sauce/ketchup and mix well.

Add 1/4 cup water and salt, and mix well. Add the marinated chicken pieces and combine so they're coated with the masala. Once the chicken starts changing color, add another 1/2 cup water and mix well.

Bring to a boil, reduce the flame, cover, and cook until the chicken is done, stirring occasionally and adding more water only if needed. Once cooked, remove the lid, add a bit more curry leaves, and continue cooking uncovered for another 5-7 minutes on low flame to roast it a little more. Remove from heat - the dish will darken further as it rests.

R0239.title: Kerala Style Pepper Chicken

1 tablespoon ghee or coconut oil, plus more for greasing
ingredients.item: ghee or coconut oil, plus more for greasing

instructions.text: Rinse the uncooked rice a couple of times, then soak it in water for 4-6 hours or overnight.
Drain the rice and blend it with the cooked rice, grated coconut, and enough cold water to make a smooth batter.
Dissolve the teaspoon of sugar in the warm water, stir in the yeast, and let it proof for about 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the proofed yeast and the remaining sugar into the rice batter, then let it ferment for 4-6 hours or overnight until airy and risen.
Once fermented, mix the salt, ground cardamom, and ground cumin into the batter, tasting and adjusting the sugar and salt to preference.
Optionally, melt about a tablespoon of ghee in a small pan and lightly fry the cashews and raisins until the cashew edges turn golden; this step can be skipped.
Pour the batter into a ghee-greased pan (a 10-inch steel pan or an idli steamer works) until about three-quarters full, then sprinkle the cashews and raisins on top.
Steam for 15-20 minutes, until the vattayappam is springy and firm to the touch.
Let it cool before removing from the pan and slicing to serve.

R0370.title: Kerala Vattayappam

ingredients.rawText: 4 ounces deveined and cleaned shrimp, chopped

instructions.text: Put the chopped shrimp, clam, and squid into a bowl. Add the green chili pepper, green onion, carrot, flour, potato starch, egg, water, fish sauce, kosher salt, black pepper, and toasted sesame oil, and mix everything together with a spoon.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add about 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil and swirl to coat evenly.
Spoon 1 or 2 scoops of the mixture onto the skillet and shape into round, 1/2-inch thick, about 3-inch wide disks. Add more disks until the skillet is comfortably full.

R0137.title: Seafood Pancakes

1 1/2 tsp dried thyme or rosemary (or 2.5 tsp finely chopped fresh)
2 cups / 500 ml braising liquid from slow cooker, strained (gravy)

instructions.text: Place the lamb in the slow cooker or on a work surface. Sprinkle with salt, pepper, thyme or rosemary, and garlic. Drizzle over the oil and rub it into both sides.

R0055.title: Slow Cooker Roast Lamb Leg with Gravy

instructions.text: Rinse the aval (flattened/beaten rice) well 2-3 times, then drain completely. Let it sit for 10 minutes. Any variety of aval works, thin or thick; if using a thick variety, sprinkle a bit of water after draining and let it sit 15-20 minutes instead. Make sure the aval turns soft.
Heat 1/4 cup of water and dissolve the jaggery in it, then filter to remove any impurities.
Boil the filtered jaggery water until it reaches one-string consistency, then continue boiling 3-4 more minutes until thick. Switch off the flame.
Add the cardamom powder and the softened aval to the jaggery syrup and mix well, then stir in the grated coconut.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews until golden brown, then mix them into the aval mixture.

For the dry coating: combine the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl and whisk until even. Whisk in the reserved marinade until the mixture forms coarse, mealy clumps. Set aside.

ingredients.rawText: 15 oz / 425 g canned sardines in tomato sauce
3 oz / 85 g (1 small) red onion, finely chopped
2 green chiles, slit in half lengthwise
ingredients.item: green chiles, slit in half lengthwise

ingredients.rawText: 4 tablespoons coconut oil or vegetable oil

instructions.text: Remove the sardines from the can and set aside in a bowl, leaving the tomato sauce in the can (about 1/4 cup).

Heat the coconut oil in a pot. Add the onion and saute for one minute. Add the ginger, garlic, green chiles, and 1/4 teaspoon salt; saute until golden brown. Add the fenugreek, turmeric, coriander, and red chili powder, and saute for 20 seconds on low heat so the spices lose their rawness without burning.

Turn the heat to medium. Add the reserved tomato sauce and stir; cook a few minutes until reduced and thick, until the raw tomato taste is gone. Add the water and 1/4 teaspoon salt, stir, and bring to a boil, tasting and adding more salt if needed. Reduce heat to low, add the sardines, and gently separate the fish so it lies flat in the sauce. Add a sprig of curry leaves, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes.

After the first 4 minutes, gently swirl the covered pot and continue cooking the remaining 4 minutes. Turn off the heat, tear up a few curry leaves and add them to the pot, cover, and swirl gently. The curry tastes better the longer it sits; eat right away or let it rest at least 30 minutes if you have the patience.

R0133.title: Daifuku Mochi

ingredients.rawText: 3/4 cup shiratamako (glutinous rice flour/sweet rice flour) (or 3/4 cup mochiko as a substitute)
ingredients.item: shiratamako (glutinous rice flour/sweet rice flour), or substitute mochiko

ingredients.rawText: 1/4 cup sugar (do not omit; it helps the mochi stay soft)
1 1/2 cups sweet red bean paste (anko), preferably tsubuan (chunky style)
ingredients.item: sweet red bean paste (anko), preferably tsubuan (chunky style)

instructions.text: Gather all the ingredients. Note that this recipe needs 15 minutes of chilling time later on.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the shiratamako and sugar until combined.
Add the water and mix well until combined.

Microwave method: loosely cover the bowl with plastic wrap and microwave on high (1100W) for 1 minute. Remove and stir with a wet rubber spatula. Cover loosely again and microwave 1 more minute, stir again, then cover and microwave 30 seconds more. The mochi should turn from white to almost translucent.

Steaming method (alternative to the microwave): wrap the steamer lid with a towel so condensation doesn't drip into the mixture, then steam the covered bowl for 15 minutes, stirring with a wet rubber spatula halfway through. The mochi should turn from white to almost translucent.
Cover a work surface with parchment paper and dust generously with potato starch. Transfer the hot mochi onto it.

Dust the top of the mochi with more potato starch to keep it from sticking. Once it has cooled slightly, spread it into a thin layer (about 3/16 inch / 4-5 mm) using your hands or a rolling pin dusted with potato starch.
Transfer the mochi, still on its parchment paper, to a large baking sheet and refrigerate for 15 minutes (no longer) until set.
Remove the chilled mochi from the refrigerator and cut out 7-8 circles using a 3 1/2-inch (9 cm) cookie cutter or round bowl.

Brush the excess potato starch off the wrappers with a pastry brush, dusting and re-brushing any sticky spots. Stack the wrappers between layers of plastic wrap on a plate. Gather the leftover dough scraps, roll them out again, and cut additional circles - you should end up with about 12 wrappers total.
On the work surface, lay out one sheet of plastic wrap with a mochi wrapper on top. Using a cookie scoop, place a scoop of anko in the center of the wrapper.
Pinch four opposite points of the mochi circle together to enclose the filling, then pinch the remaining edges together to seal it fully.

Dust the sealed area with a little potato starch and set the daifuku aside, seam side down. Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling. Store in a cool, dry place (or the refrigerator in summer) and enjoy within two days.

In a medium bowl sift together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Set it aside.
In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, beat together butter and sugars for 2-3 minutes until light and
fluffy. Add honey and beat for one more minute. Scrape down the sides and the bottom of the bowl occasionally.
On medium speed, beat in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add mashed bananas and

combined. Add the yogurt and beat until combined. Add the other half of the dry ingredients and beat slowly or
fold by hand just until combined. Do not overmix — the less you mix, the lighter the bread will be. Fold in the nuts. |

bread comes out clean or with just a few moist crumbs. Let the bread cool for 10 minutes on a wire rack, then
turn it out from the pan and let it cool completely.
Notes
Store the bread at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
The bread can be frozen for up to 2 months. Thaw it on the counter, still covered, or overnight in the fridge.

ingredients.rawText: 1 lb (450 g) lamb leg, cut to 2/3-inch (1.5-cm) cubes
1 tablespoon soy sauce (or tamari for gluten free)

ingredients.item: Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry for gluten free)

ingredients.item: Sichuan chili flakes (or Korean chili flakes)

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup whole dried Chinese chili peppers (or Korean chili peppers)
ingredients.item: whole dried Chinese chili peppers (or Korean chili peppers)

instructions.text: Combine the lamb, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and salt in a large bowl. Mix well and marinate at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to overnight in the fridge.
Stir together the cumin powder, chili flakes, sugar, and Sichuan peppercorns in a small bowl to make the spice mix.
When ready to cook, drain any excess liquid from the lamb. Add the cornstarch and stir until every piece is coated.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until hot. Spread the lamb out with tongs so the pieces don't overlap. Sear without touching until the bottom turns golden, about 1 minute, then flip and cook the other side until slightly golden while the inside stays a bit pink, 30-40 seconds. Transfer the lamb to a plate.

If needed, add more oil to the pan so about 2 tablespoons remain. Add the dried chili peppers, onion, ginger, and garlic; stir and cook about 1 minute until the onion starts to turn tender. Return the lamb to the pan and sprinkle the spice mix over everything, stirring immediately to coat. Taste a piece and add more salt if needed.
Add the cilantro and give everything a final stir, then transfer immediately to a plate.
Serve hot with steamed rice, garnished with toasted sesame seeds if desired.

instructions.text: If making your own noodles, prepare the dough fully before starting the lamb stir-fry, and set a pot of water to boil so it's ready as soon as the lamb is done.

Toast the cumin, Sichuan peppercorns, and coriander in a dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring often, about 5 minutes until fragrant and starting to pop. Grind partially (mortar and pestle, spice grinder, coffee grinder, or crushed with the bottom of a heavy pan).
Combine the lamb with the Shaoxing wine, salt, oil, and 2 teaspoons of the ground spices. Mix in the cornstarch by hand until the lamb is fully coated. Marinate for 15 minutes.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat until it begins to smoke. Add the marinated lamb in a single layer, separating the slices with tongs or chopsticks. Top with the garlic and ginger and sear 30 seconds to a minute until the bottom browns.
Stir occasionally until the lamb is mostly browned on both sides and the aromatics turn golden; it's fine if the inside is still a bit pink.
Add the red onion and green chili and stir-fry for 10-20 seconds.
Add the remaining spice mix and toss to coat everything.
Pour in the sauce, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan, and stir-fry another 30 seconds.
Turn off the heat, stir in the cilantro, and transfer everything to a plate so the lamb stops cooking.

Boil the noodles: for hand-pulled noodles, stretch and drop each piece into the boiling water and cook 1-2 minutes; for packaged noodles, cook according to the package instructions. Divide the cooked noodles among 4 bowls.
Top the noodles with the lamb and sauce. Add extra chili oil, chinkiang vinegar, or soy sauce to taste and serve.

instructions.text: Toast the chilies: heat a wok or small saucepan over low heat, add half the oil, and add the fresh and dried peppers. Stir occasionally and heat about 5 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Remove from heat and set aside. (Skip this if using homemade toasted chili oil.)

Heat the remaining oil in the wok over medium heat, then raise the heat to high and add the ground pork. Break it up and fry until cooked through. Add the ground Sichuan peppercorns and stir for about 15-30 seconds, taking care not to let them burn or turn bitter.
Stir in the spicy bean sauce, then add the chicken broth and let it simmer for a minute or so. Meanwhile, prepare the tofu and combine the water and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Add the cornstarch mixture to the sauce and stir. Let it bubble until it starts to thicken, thinning with a splash more water or broth if it gets too thick.

Stir in the reserved chili oil and peppers (if using homemade chili oil, use only the standing oil, not the sediment, to avoid extra salt). Add the tofu and gently toss to coat in the sauce. Cook 3-5 minutes, then stir in the sesame oil and sugar, if using, along with the scallions, until the scallions are just wilted.
Serve with a final sprinkle of Sichuan peppercorn powder as garnish, if desired.

instructions.text: In a medium bowl, add the Greek yogurt.
Press or finely mince the garlic directly into the yogurt (the press gives the
smoothest integration).
Add the finely chopped fresh mint, lemon juice, kosher salt, black pepper,
and the pinch of cayenne.
Whisk everything together vigorously until smooth and well combined. The
sauce should be creamy with flecks of green mint.
Taste and adjust: add a little more lemon juice for brightness, more salt if
needed, or a touch more cayenne if you want subtle heat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 15-20 minutes (or up to a few hours) so the
flavors meld. It will thicken slightly in the fridge.
Serving tips
Serve chilled or at cool room temperature alongside the sliced lamb.
It cuts the richness of the roasted lamb beautifully and also pairs nicely with
the crispy Greek lemon potatoes.
If it thickens too much in the fridge, stir in a teaspoon of water or extra lemon
juice to loosen it.
That's it—super simple, fresh, and classic with lamb. Enjoy your Easter feast! Let me know if you
want any adjustments (e.g., adding cucumber for a tzatziki twist or making it dairy-free).

ingredients.item: boneless chicken, rinsed and cleaned, cut into cubes

ingredients.rawText: 2 teaspoons Garam Masala Powder (or Curry Powder)
ingredients.item: garam masala powder (or curry powder), optional

instructions.text: Rinse the chicken and cut it into bite-size cubes; place in a large bowl.
Toss the chicken with the salt and lemon juice and let it sit in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine the first-marinade ingredients in a bowl: cashew paste, ginger paste, garlic paste, cornstarch, green cardamom powder, crushed green chilies, cumin powder, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt.

In a separate bowl, combine the second set of ingredients: hung curd/yogurt, mozzarella, kasoori methi, cilantro, cream, and oil. Omit the cilantro, green chilies, or garam masala if you prefer a milder tikka.
Combine both marinade mixtures together in one large bowl and mix well, tasting and adjusting seasoning as needed.
Add the marinated chicken to the combined mixture and toss until every piece is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for 5-6 hours, or ideally overnight.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers, dividing evenly among about 6 skewers.

instructions.text: Rinse the pork chops under running water and lightly scrub with salt, then pat dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, stir together the sugar, soy sauce, fish sauce, MSG, and oil until the sugar and MSG dissolve, then mix in the minced lemongrass, garlic, and shallots.
Marinate the pork chops in this mixture, covered, in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight.
Remove the chops from the fridge about an hour before cooking. Lift them out of the marinade and discard the excess liquid, keeping any aromatics that cling to the meat.
To grill: sear on high heat until browned with good grill marks, then move to medium heat and cook, flipping often, until the internal temperature reaches 145 degrees F.
To pan-fry: cook 1-2 chops at a time over medium-high heat without crowding the pan, until they reach 145 degrees F internally.

To bake: roast at 375 degrees F for 15-20 minutes until the chops reach about 135 degrees F internally, then lower the rack and broil, flipping a few times, until browned and the internal temperature hits 145 degrees F.
Serve the pork chops with white rice, the sliced tomato, cucumber, lettuce, and scallion oil, alongside a bowl of dipping fish sauce (nuoc cham) for drizzling.
